A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NaturalGAIA and LightManus, retaining the 276-task benchmark and core evaluation metrics. All supplied pages are readable. However, v1 references Appendices A–C that are absent from its nine-page PDF, limiting comparison of earlier construction, trajectory and training details. V3 includes Appendices A–F.

before.justification: V1 reports original NaturalGAIA evaluations, Qwen2.5-VL-7B fine-tuning results, A3 generalization results and failure analyses in Tables 1–2 and Figure 2.

after.justification: V3 reports original architecture comparisons, efficiency measurements, failure analyses, AndroidWorld evaluations and browser-only comparisons in Tables 2–3 and 7–8 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: V1 delegates execution to Mobile-Agent-e/PC-Agent and proposes trajectory-based reinforcement fine-tuning. V3 introduces Jarvis with screenshot/accessibility-tree fusion, filtered element identifiers and identifier-based Android actions; fine-tuning disappears from the reported method. Hierarchical decomposition and dynamic scheduling remain underlying components.

E1.justification: The reported study removes the trajectory-training corpus and A3 evaluation on six unseen-application subsets. V3 adds AndroidWorld and a browser-only NaturalGAIA scenario in Appendix E. The benchmark remains described as 276 tasks; the PDFs do not establish which individual tasks were regenerated.

E2.justification: V3 adds UI-TARS-1.5-7B to the main comparison, M3A on AndroidWorld and Mind2Web on the browser-only subset. PC-Agent and Mobile-Agent-e remain named comparators. However, PC-Agent's citation changes from Liu et al. (2025b) to a different work by He et al. (2024b), leaving that comparator's continuity uncertain.

E3.justification: Backends change substantially, including GPT-o3 to GPT-5.2 and Claude-Sonnet-4 to 4.5, with Gemini-3 and newer Qwen configurations added. New protocols include matched-backend external comparisons and efficiency measurement across five shared Level-3 tasks using Gemini-3.0-Flash. Newly disclosed emulator specifications alone do not establish an environment change.

E4.justification: V3 extends the existing MAe/LightManus comparison with a Jarvis executor ablation and adds token/time analysis. RFT-focused diagnostics are replaced by architecture/backend failure comparisons, illustrated error cases in Appendix F and generalization tests of the revised framework.

E5.justification: Both versions report Pass@1 and, where available, Pass@4 without seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. V3's five-task efficiency averages specify an evaluation sample rather than introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported values change even for retained labels: MAe with Gemini-2.5-Pro has overall WPSR 23.2% in v1 Table 1 and 21.1% in v3 Table 2. V3 adds Jarvis, efficiency and external-test results while removing RFT/A3 results. The headline 34.6% versus 45.6% uses different model/executor combinations and does not establish a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: Changes concern methodological definitions: v3 formalizes application information spaces, constrained graph-walk steps and Jarvis's observation/action mapping, while v1's training-trajectory tuple disappears. The WPSR, MATCR and positional success-rate equations remain equivalent. Neither supplied PDF contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes a human-verified trajectory dataset, reinforcement fine-tuning and smaller models' capability ceilings. V3 replaces those central contributions with logic–language separation and the LightManus-Jarvis architecture, claiming stronger execution and substantially lower token/time costs. This changes the paper's scientific focus.

C2.justification: Interpretation shifts from fine-tuning's benefits and limitations to semantic drift, hybrid perception, reasoning–execution tradeoffs and cumulative errors. V3 also explicitly identifies restricted task diversity, exclusion of dynamic/irreversible scenarios, human-verification bottlenecks and inference-induced state drift; v1's limitations discussion is substantially narrower.

D1.justification: V3 supplies a code-access URL, emulator/VM specifications, accessibility-tree and action implementation details, knowledge-graph construction and verification procedures, and an execution listing. V1's trajectory-curation and four-A100 training disclosures disappear with the training study. Earlier details deferred to missing appendices cannot be checked.

R1.justification: Positioning moves from trajectory-data scarcity and experiential learning toward realistic verifiable evaluation, context management and hybrid execution. V3 adds substantial discussion and citations around OSWorld, UI-TARS, agentic context engineering and hierarchical planning, plus a systematic benchmark comparison in Table 6.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the revised contribution. Benchmark subsections are reorganized, the trajectory-training sections disappear, and a separate limitations section and structured appendices substantially alter the document's organization.

P2.justification: V3 redraws the architecture diagram, replaces the failure pie charts with a radar chart and restructures the main results table. It adds construction diagrams, observation-space and efficiency tables, appendix comparison tables, task examples, screenshots and a formatted execution listing.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's underspecified fine-tuning procedure and missing referenced appendices, v3 makes benchmark construction and execution substantially easier to audit. Component comparisons, efficiency measurements and explicit applicability limits strengthen support for its revised contribution. Reporting weaknesses remain: Section 5.2 claims a Gemini-3 Flash WPSR advantage although Table 2 shows an 81.2% tie with Pro, and uncertainty estimates remain absent. These weaknesses temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in transparency and empirical support.
